DS-01.name: The twins that aren't
DS-01.orient: Two bright white stars were logged as twins because they look alike in the eyepiece. Appearance is a starting observation, not identity.
DS-01.notice: Look at both targets. Read the inherited log. If the eyepiece is not enough, the basin still has a known light south of the dome.
DS-01.reason: A spectrum is a record of structure in the light. Two objects can look the same and still leave different traces.
DS-01.teach: Visible color and brightness do not prove two stars are the same kind. A known lamp gives a repeatable pattern you can compare against stellar traces.
DS-01.scaffold: Walk to Lamp Bench for a fair reference, then bring that pattern back to the plate spectrograph. Try to align the two stellar traces. Log what refuses to match.
explainMore: Looking the same from far away does not prove much. I should know.
The lamp is not a lecture. It is a light you can test because you already know the source.

misconceptions.eyepiece-twins: If they look white and bright, they still might not be the same light. The traces have to agree.
misconceptions.spectrum-quiz: This is not a vocabulary match. You are comparing patterns you recorded.

DS-01.worldCue: The dome wash is the problem. The lamp is south of here, on purpose.

DS-02.name: The cooler ember
DS-02.orient: The old notes treat a reddish star as an ember, like a hot coal. Color folklore is not a temperature measurement.
DS-02.notice: Compare the reddish target with a white one you already logged. Watch where each trace is brightest, not only the color you saw.
DS-02.reason: A peak sitting farther toward longer wavelength is not evidence that the source is hotter.
DS-02.teach: Visible redness is one observation. Peak position is another. Temperature inference has to follow the evidence you actually marked.
DS-02.scaffold: Slide the peak marker to each trace's brightest place. Use the wavelength marks, not color memory.
explainMore: Fire-color folklore is stubborn. The trace does not care what a coal looks like.
I will not invent a temperature you did not measure.

misconceptions.red-hotter: Red as fire is a story. Peak position is the evidence on this bench.
misconceptions.color-only: Color without a peak mark is not enough here.

DS-02.worldCue: The reddish target is still in the same sky. The spectrograph can hold both traces.
